method: Relevant formation and use sections read in independent authored teaching sources. Original examples, conversations and prose; publisher examples and exam items not copied. Restricted JMdict matching verifies 54 written/reading pairs, not official JLPT level or naturalness.

points.formation: Negative base + ぬ; する→せぬ, 来る→こぬ. Classical ず attributive remnant; marked modern terminal uses also occur.
points.teachingChoice: Literary/fixed recognition, not ordinary friend-chat production. Do not assert every written ぬ negates; contrast completion separately.

points.formation: Negative base + ざる + noun; する→せざる, 来る→こざる.
points.teachingChoice: Unknown sender/town in an old letter. Distinguish restricted literary negative modification from the whole modern pattern ざるを得ない. Publisher level labels differ; course placement is recognition sequencing.

points.form: べからず / べからざる
points.formation: Dictionary verb + べからず; marked する→す also recognised. Restricted attributive べからざる + noun.
points.teachingChoice: Quoted old standing sign, current bridge repair notice and an actual alternate garden route. 欠くべからざる means indispensable, not a ban on the following object. No universal ban on quoting a written sign aloud.

points.form: ごとし / ごとく / ごとき
points.formation: Predicate ごとし; adverbial ごとく; noun-modifying ごとき. Nの / contextual V or かの frame.
points.teachingChoice: Water/reflection and fish-like shadow comparisons do not mean literal transformation. Direct person+ごとき can belittle; neutral likeness is not universally insulting. NihongoNET table typo not adopted.

points.form: Classical completion ぬ versus negative ぬ
points.formation: Completion ぬ follows 連用形; negative remnant follows 未然形. 雨やみぬ contrasts with 雨やまぬ; classical 来ぬ may be きぬ or こぬ.
points.teachingChoice: Zkai own publisher PDF zero-based pages 5 and 7 inspected in extracted text: connection table and ambiguity explanation. Some stems coincide; context and larger grammar matter. This is a limited recognition bridge, not a full classical grammar course.
